note: PHASE 4 -- ARC CLOSE. R5 generalises what P2's follow-up (#238) did by hand in one file. Measured on this tree at authoring time, 90 check-/lint- scripts: 14 carry a canary and 13 of those never call the function owning their exit code, so flipping a `return 2` to `return 0` left every one of their rule cases green. R3, the rule that CLAIMS the 0/1/2 contract, has zero allowlist entries -- but that zero is evidence about 62 scripts, not 90, and nothing distinguishes it from evidence about all of them. Measured: 66 carry the literal `if (!url || !key)` shape R3 matches; 62 of those pair it with process.exit(2) and are genuinely measured compliant; the other 4 spell the code as `return 2`, which R3 -- pairing its shape with process.exit(N) only -- sees as an `if` followed by no exit call, so it declines to hit. 6 scripts in total return their codes rather than exiting them. (The header first said 'all 66 exit 2'; a review measured it at 62 + 4 and this is the corrected figure.) R5 asks whether the contract is DRIVEN rather than matching a shape, so it cannot be spelled around. R5 IS ANSWERED ON A TYPESCRIPT AST, not by scanning text, and that was forced by measurement rather than taste: two review rounds found six defects in the hand-rolled scanner, the last of them fail-OPEN and live in this tree -- with no keyword denylist, `if (` in the statement after a semicolon-free `process.exitCode = code` was collected as an exit owner, and since nearly every canary body contains an `if (`, the rule reported CLEAN on a canary that drove nothing (check-sourcemap-debugids.mjs already yielded owners ['if','main'], firing only by luck). Each patch closed an instance and left the class, because text scanning cannot answer a question about SCOPE. typescript is already a direct dependency and already used this way by scripts/check-wallclock-brand.mjs, so this added no dependency and no new precedent; the swap deleted every hand-rolled primitive (matchDelimiter, skipSpace, bindings, calledIn, isNameChar) and the allowlist baseline came out BYTE-IDENTICAL -- the same 12 files, no additions, no stale -- which is the evidence that the parser agrees with the scanner everywhere the scanner was right. R1-R4 stay on regex; they match shapes, not scope. Proven in both directions over 64 canary cases and a 25-mutant pass: 24 real mutants all killed, plus one deliberately unparseable control that must be -- and is -- reported INCONCLUSIVE rather than survived, because a mutant that fails to parse prints zero FAIL lines and reads exactly like a survivor, which produced a false finding in an earlier session. Three defects were found BY THE MUTATION PASS rather than by reading: main() never proved it AWAITED its canary (unawaited, selfTest returns a Promise, which is truthy, so a FAILING self-test exited 0 and the CI step went green -- now a boolean is required and a non-boolean verdict is exit 2); the harness itself used execFileSync, which discards stderr on a zero exit, where the verdict line is printed, so it misreported a killed mutant as never reaching a verdict; and CRLF checkout made every multi-line anchor silently match nothing, i.e. three mutants were never applied at all. Three /code-review rounds then found 28 more, all fixed before commit rather than as follow-ups. Round one: two false negatives where canaryBody() latched onto the CLI tail (a brace-less arrow canary, and an unclosed body falling back to the rest of the file), plus the header census being wrong. Round two (11 angles, every finding executed rather than read): the live keyword fail-open above, which is what triggered the AST rewrite, plus a rejection out of main() landing as exit 1 -- 'a convention was violated' -- for an unreadable scripts/ dir that measured nothing, now caught inside main() and mapped to 2; a duplicate per-file diagnose pass costing ~15% of scan time, now read off the hit; and the R4 -> R5 promotion printing 'a NEW guard script can report green without checking' at an author who had just PAID DOWN R4 debt, now named as a promotion. Known and deliberately NOT fixed here, because it is pre-existing and tree-wide rather than this diff's: the `if (IS_CLI)` realpath compare mispredicts through a junction or symlink and exits 0 having run nothing -- 8 of 8 sibling guards share it, the repo already removed it once in check-og-images.mjs, and it wants its own change. CLAUDE.md no longer claims the canary drives the CLI; it drives main(). Round three audited the REWRITE and found the same class had followed it in: this file's own new CLI tail made `String` an exit owner (from String(error) in a .catch formatter) and the file passed R5 only because a canary helper coincidentally calls String() -- 'fires only by luck', the exact charge the header lays against the text scanner. Fixed by making the owner walk structural: it visits only value-producing positions and never an argument, so main(parseArgs(argv)) owns main alone. Round three also moved the crash handler out of the undriven `if (IS_CLI)` tail into main(), because a tail handler that stops returning an integer sets process.exitCode = undefined and node exits 0 -- a crashed guard reporting green -- and it is now driven by a case; plus destructured `const { code } = await main()` and a nested-helper local no longer misread as not-drivable and as a shadow.
